paper.title: Lattice dynamics in mono- and few-layer sheets of WS2 and WSe2
paper.abstract: Thickness is one of the fundamental parameters that define the electronic, optical, and thermal properties of two-dimensional (2D) crystals. Phonons in molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) were recently found to exhibit unique thickness dependence due to interplay between short and long range interactions. Here we report Raman spectra of atomically thin sheets of WS2 and WSe2 in the mono- to few-layer thickness regime. We show that, similar to the case of MoS2, the characteristic and modes exhibit stiffening and softening with increasing number of layers, respectively, with a small shift of less than 3 cm-1 due to large mass of the atoms. Thickness dependence is also observed in a series of multiphonon bands arising from overtone, combination, and zone edge phonons, whose intensity exhibit significant enhancement in excitonic resonance conditions. Some of these multiphonon peaks are found to be absent only in monolayers. These features provide a unique fingerprint and rapid identification for monolayer flakes.

paper.title: Excitation energy dependence of Raman spectra of few-layer WS2
paper.abstract: Raman spectra of few-layer WS2 have been measured with up to seven excitation energies, and peculiar resonance effects are observed. The two-phonon acoustic phonon scattering signal close to the main E2g1 peak is stronger than the main peaks for excitations near the A or B exciton states. The low-frequency Raman spectra show a series of shear and layer-breathing modes that are useful for determining the number of layers. In addition, hitherto unidentified peaks (X1 and X2), which do not seem to depend on the layer thickness, are observed near resonances with exciton states. The polarization dependences of the two peaks are different: X1 vanishes in cross polarization, but X2 does not. At the resonance with the A exciton state, the Raman-forbidden, lowest-frequency shear mode for odd number of layers appears as strong as that for the allowed case of even number of layers. This mode also exhibits a strong Breit-Wigner-Fano line shape and an anomalous polarization behavior at this resonance.

paper.title: Second order resonant Raman scattering in single layer tungsten disulfide (WS$_{2}$)
paper.abstract: Resonant Raman spectra of single layer WS$_{2}$ flakes are presented. A second order Raman peak (2LA) appears under resonant excitation with a separation from the E$^{1}_{2g}$ mode of only $4$cm$^{-1}$. Depending on the intensity ratio and the respective line widths of these two peaks, any analysis which neglects the presence of the 2LA mode can lead to an inaccurate estimation of the position of the E$^{1}_{2g}$ mode, leading to a potentially incorrect assignment for the number of layers. Our results show that the intensity of the 2LA mode strongly depends on the angle between the linear polarization of the excitation and detection, a parameter which is neglected in many Raman studies.

papers.title: Determining layer number of two dimensional flakes of transition-metal dichalcogenides by the Raman intensity from substrate
papers.abstract: Transition-metal dichalcogenide (TMD) semiconductors have been widely studied due to their distinctive electronic and optical properties. The property of TMD flakes is a function of its thickness, or layer number (N). How to determine N of ultrathin TMDs materials is of primary importance for fundamental study and practical applications. Raman mode intensity from substrates has been used to identify N of intrinsic and defective multilayer graphenes up to N=100. However, such analysis is not applicable for ultrathin TMD flakes due to the lack of a unified complex refractive index ($\tilde{n}$) from monolayer to bulk TMDs. Here, we discuss the N identification of TMD flakes on the SiO$_2$/Si substrate by the intensity ratio between the Si peak from 100-nm (or 89-nm) SiO$_2$/Si substrates underneath TMD flakes and that from bare SiO$_2$/Si substrates. We assume the real part of $\tilde{n}$ of TMD flakes as that of monolayer TMD and treat the imaginary part of $\tilde{n}$ as a fitting parameter to fit the experimental intensity ratio. An empirical $\tilde{n}$, namely, $\tilde{n}_{eff}$, of ultrathin MoS$_{2}$, WS$_{2}$ and WSe$_{2}$ flakes from monolayer to multilayer is obtained for typical laser excitations (2.54 eV, 2.34 eV, or 2.09 eV). The fitted $\tilde{n}_{eff}$ of MoS$_{2}$ has been used to identify N of MoS$_{2}$ flakes deposited on 302-nm SiO$_2$/Si substrate, which agrees well with that determined from their shear and layer-breathing modes. This technique by measuring Raman intensity from the substrate can be extended to identify N of ultrathin 2D flakes with N-dependent $\tilde{n}$ . For the application purpose, the intensity ratio excited by specific laser excitations has been provided for MoS$_{2}$, WS$_{2}$ and WSe$_{2}$ flakes and multilayer graphene flakes deposited on Si substrates covered by 80-110 nm or 280-310 nm SiO$_2$ layer.

papers.title: Second order resonant Raman scattering in single layer tungsten disulfide (WS$_{2}$)
papers.abstract: Resonant Raman spectra of single layer WS$_{2}$ flakes are presented. A second order Raman peak (2LA) appears under resonant excitation with a separation from the E$^{1}_{2g}$ mode of only $4$cm$^{-1}$. Depending on the intensity ratio and the respective line widths of these two peaks, any analysis which neglects the presence of the 2LA mode can lead to an inaccurate estimation of the position of the E$^{1}_{2g}$ mode, leading to a potentially incorrect assignment for the number of layers. Our results show that the intensity of the 2LA mode strongly depends on the angle between the linear polarization of the excitation and detection, a parameter which is neglected in many Raman studies.

papers.title: Raman spectroscopy of the interlayer shear mode in few-layer MoS2 flakes
papers.abstract: Single- and few-layer MoS2 has recently gained attention as an interesting new material system for opto-electronics. Here, we report on scanning Raman measurements on few-layer MoS2 flakes prepared by exfoliation. We observe a Raman mode corresponding to a rigid shearing oscillation of adjacent layers. This mode appears at very low Raman shifts between 20 and 30 relative wavenumbers. Its position strongly depends on the number of layers, which we independently determine using AFM measurements and investigation of the other characteristic Raman modes. Raman spectroscopy of the shear mode therefore is a useful tool to determine the number of layers for few-layer MoS2 flakes.

papers.title: Substrate-free layer-number identification of two-dimensional materials: A case of Mo$_{0.5}$W$_{0.5}$S$_2$ alloy
papers.abstract: Any of two or more two-dimensional (2D) materials with similar properties can be alloyed into a new layered material, namely, 2D alloy. Individual monolayer in 2D alloys are kept together by Van der Waals interactions. The property of multilayer alloys is a function of their layer number. Here, we studied the shear (C) and layer-breathing (LB) modes of Mo$_{0.5}$W$_{0.5}$S$_2$ alloy flakes and their link to the layer number of alloy flakes. The study reveals that the disorder effect is absent in the C and LB modes of 2D alloys, and the monatomic chain model can be used to estimate the frequencies of the C and LB modes. We demonstrated how to use the C and LB mode frequency to identify the layer number of alloy flakes deposited on different substrates. This technique is independent of the substrate, stoichiometry, monolayer thickness and complex refractive index of 2D materials, offering a robust and substrate-free approach for layer-number identification of 2D materials.

papers.title: Splitting of the monolayer out-of-plane A'1 Raman mode in few-layer WS2
papers.abstract: We present Raman measurements of mono- and few-layer WS2. We study the monolayer A'1 mode around 420 cm(-1) and its evolution with the number of layers. We show that with increasing layer number there is an increasing number of possible vibrational patterns for the out-of-plane Raman mode: in N-layer WS2 there are N Gamma-point phonons evolving from the A'1 monolayer mode. For an excitation energy close to resonance with the excitonic transition energy we were able to observe all of these N components, irrespective of their Raman activity. Density functional theory calculations support the experimental findings and make it possible to attribute the modes to their respective symmetries. The findings described here are of general importance for all other phonon modes in WS2 and other layered transition metal dichalcogenide systems in the few layer regime.

structured_output.summary: Both spots are 2H-WS2 (E-type band near 355 cm-1 and A1 band at 417 to 420 cm-1, with the 2LA(M) overtone near 350 cm-1). Spot 1 is thinner than spot 2: its out-of-plane A1 band is 2.8 cm-1 softer, its A1-E separation is 61.9 vs 64.7 cm-1, and its Si substrate line is about 10x stronger. The data are consistent with a monolayer or few-layer island, but they do not establish a monolayer. The strongest layer-number observables (shear and layer-breathing modes below 50 cm-1) are outside the measured window (starts at 120 cm-1), and no polarization or PL data are available. The skill's helper scripts and reference notes sit outside this folder, so per the folder restriction I did all fits with numpy/scipy here.

observations.finding: Spot 1 peak table (global 5-band Lorentzian fit over 140-560 cm-1 with linear baseline; fit errors only): LA(M) 175.95±0.24 cm-1 (FWHM 9.2±0.8, amp 113); 2LA(M) 351.18±0.04 (FWHM 9.15±0.06, amp 1828); E2g/E' 355.34±0.06 (FWHM 3.55±0.28, amp 374); A1g/A1' 417.28±0.02 (FWHM 4.65±0.07, amp 806); Si 520.91±0.01 (FWHM 3.45±0.04, amp 1235).
observations.evidence: spectrum_spot1.csv, 698 points, 120.00-599.94 cm-1, step about 0.69 cm-1. Residual rms 13.2 overall (E-region 12.5, A-region 14.2, LA-region 12.9).
spectrum_spot2.csv, 732 points, 120.00-599.56 cm-1. Residual rms 14.5 overall (E-region 14.3, A-region 11.2, LA-region 12.4).

observations.finding: A single Lorentzian in the 330-375 cm-1 window leaves structure that a two-component fit removes: spot 1 window rms 34 (single) vs 12 (two components), spot 2 window rms 56 vs 14. The sharp E' component is at 355.3 (spot 1) and 355.4 cm-1 (spot 2) in the two-component fit; the broad lower component is 2LA(M) at 351.1 and 349.9 cm-1.
observations.evidence: Two-Lorentzian fit over 325-385 cm-1 with linear baseline. Spot 1: E' 355.29±0.06 (FWHM 3.95±0.29), 2LA 351.09±0.05 (FWHM 8.94±0.09), 2LA/E' amp ratio about 4.3. Spot 2: E' 355.38±0.04 (FWHM 4.12±0.15), 2LA 349.86±0.12 (FWHM 8.76±0.32), 2LA/E' amp ratio about 0.8.

observations.finding: Delta(A1g-E2g) = 61.94±0.07 cm-1 in spot 1 and 64.66±0.04 cm-1 in spot 2 (difference 2.7 cm-1). The A1 band shifts by +2.80 cm-1 from spot 1 to spot 2, while the E' band shifts by only about +0.07 cm-1 (about 0.08 with the separate fit).
observations.evidence: Global fit positions (fit errors only). Si line positions differ by 0.12 cm-1 between spectra, so calibration offset cannot account for a 2.8 cm-1 A1 shift. Zhao et al. (Nanoscale 2013) report a thickness-dependent shift of the characteristic modes of less than 3 cm-1 for mono- to few-layer WS2, which matches the size of this shift.

observations.finding: Spot 1 is consistent with a thinner flake than spot 2 (monolayer or few-layer), but a monolayer is not established. A thin island would be expected to give the more consistent reading: lower A1 frequency, smaller Delta, and stronger Si.
observations.evidence: A1 red-shift of 2.8 cm-1 (about 40 times the fit error and about 10 times the calibration scatter); Delta 61.9 vs 64.7 cm-1, the separation trend reported for WS2 in layer number; Si amplitude ratio about 10.7x (1235 vs 115), consistent with less overlayer absorption for the thinner spot. The Delta-to-layer-number thresholds were not verified from source text (see limits).

observations.finding: Strong 2LA(M) in both spots, with a much larger 2LA/E' ratio in spot 1 (about 4.3-4.9) than in spot 2 (about 0.8). Resonant 2LA appears in monolayer WS2 about 4 cm-1 from E' and can bias the layer assignment if it is not fitted out.
observations.evidence: Two-Lorentzian and global fits (see rows above). The E'-to-2LA separation is about 4 cm-1 in spot 1 and about 5.5 cm-1 in spot 2. 514.5 nm = 2.41 eV, which the literature places near the WS2 A/B exciton region (Yang et al. 2017 state that the 2LA signal exceeds the main peaks near A or B exciton resonance); the exact exciton energies were not checked against a source.
observations.source: Mitioglu et al., PRB 89, 245442 (2014), arXiv [1406.3511](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.3511); Yang, Lee & Cheong (2017), arXiv [1706.01677](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.01677)

observations.finding: Same-material resonance sets the 2LA intensity, and polarization can change it independently of thickness. The 4.9 vs 0.8 ratio difference therefore cannot be read as a thickness indicator without polarization control.
observations.evidence: Mitioglu et al. report that 2LA intensity depends strongly on the angle between excitation and detection polarization.

observations.finding: A1g linewidths are similar (FWHM 4.65 vs 4.48 cm-1), so the A1 band does not broaden between spots. The E' line is also narrow in both (3.6 to 3.9 cm-1), so no clear defect-induced broadening is seen in either spot.
observations.evidence: Global fit FWHM values above; fit-error-level differences only.

observations.finding: The 175-176 cm-1 band is weak (spot 1 amp 113, spot 2 amp 45 with large uncertainty) and is assigned to LA(M). In spot 1 its amplitude is about 2.5x the E' amplitude; in spot 2 it is about 7%. This band is not a reliable layer or defect indicator from these data.
observations.evidence: Global fit LA amplitude and FWHM above; the spot 2 LA position uncertainty is 0.56 cm-1 and its FWHM 6.8±1.7 cm-1.

observations.finding: The Si line at 520.8-520.9 cm-1 is the substrate first-order line (assigned as 'Si substrate'). Its positions agree within 0.12 cm-1 and fit to a nominal calibration offset of about +0.1 to +0.2 cm-1 relative to the commonly quoted 520.7 cm-1, which is small compared with the A1 shift.
observations.evidence: Si positions 520.91±0.01 (spot 1) and 520.79±0.15 (spot 2). The nominal 520.7 cm-1 is the commonly quoted Si value; calibration source not stated in the data.

observations.finding: Phase: the mode set (E' near 355 cm-1, A1' at 417-420 cm-1, 2LA near 350 cm-1) matches 2H-WS2, consistent with the 2H phase expected for CVD WS2.
observations.evidence: Peak positions in the tables above; no 1T or 3R signature is seen in the 120-600 cm-1 window.

questions_for_user: Is there a bare SiO2/Si reference spectrum (same settings, same spot size) to calibrate the Si attenuation?
Can the spectra be re-measured below about 50 cm-1 (shear and layer-breathing modes)? These are the most direct layer-number observables and are missing because the window starts at 120 cm-1.
What were the laser power, objective, and grating/resolution? Heating shifts E' and A1' together; the A1-only shift argues against a heating-dominated result, but the power is needed to confirm.
Was polarization controlled? The 2LA/E' ratio depends on polarization, so the spot 1 vs spot 2 ratio cannot be interpreted without it.
Is there an AFM height or PL map for the island? Monolayer WS2 gives strong direct-exciton PL that thicker flakes do not; this would decide monolayer vs few-layer directly.
citations: [1304.0911](https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.0911): Zhao et al., Nanoscale 5, 9677 (2013). Mono- to few-layer WS2/WSe2; characteristic modes shift by less than 3 cm-1 with layer number; multiphonon bands enhanced under excitonic resonance.

[1406.3511](https://arxiv.org/abs/1406.3511): Mitioglu et al., PRB 89, 245442 (2014). Resonant 2LA in single-layer WS2 appears about 4 cm-1 from E^1_2g; can bias layer assignment; 2LA intensity depends on polarization angle.

[1706.01677](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.01677): Yang, Lee & Cheong (2017). 2LA signal near E2g is stronger than the main peaks near A or B exciton resonance; shear and layer-breathing modes are useful for layer number.
[1504.00049](https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.00049): Staiger et al., PRB 91, 195419 (2015). Monolayer A'1 mode near 420 cm-1 splits into N components with increasing layer number near excitonic resonance.

[1602.05378](https://arxiv.org/abs/1602.05378): Li et al., Nanotechnology 27, 145704 (2016). WS2 layer number from the Si-peak intensity ratio against bare SiO2/Si; requires a bare-substrate reference; excitation energies differ from 2.41 eV.
caveats: The skill's scripts (rl_qc, rl_fit, rl_series, rl) and the reference notes (reference/materials/WS2.md, artifacts.md, relations.md) are located outside the working folder; per the folder restriction they were not read or run. The fits were done with numpy/scipy in this folder: ALS baseline, prominence-based peak finding, and Lorentzian fits replaced the skill's QC and fit steps.

The layer-number threshold for Delta(A1g-E2g) in WS2 was not verified from source text. Only abstracts were retrieved (iopic-bond needs a token that is not set, so no figures were parsed). The statement that spot 1 is thinner rests on the direction and size of the shift and separation, not on a verified calibration curve.

The 2LA/E' ratio is sensitive to the two-component decomposition (E' amplitude 374 in the global fit vs 416 in the local E-window fit; ratio 4.9 vs 4.3). The direction (spot 1 2LA-dominated, spot 2 E'-dominated) is robust; the exact value is not.

Peak assignments for LA(M), 2LA(M), E'/E^1_2g and A1'/A1g are standard for 2H-WS2 from the literature, but the specific frequencies were not checked against a source table. Irrep labels (E^1_2g, A1g for bulk D6h; E', A1' for monolayer D3h) depend on the layer number, which is not yet established.

Alternative explanations for the A1-only shift and the Delta change: doping, strain, substrate interference, focus/spot differences, and resonance. Power/heating was not known and could add a common shift. Only one spectrum per spot was measured, so the uncertainties are fit statistics only; spot-to-spot reproducibility was not tested.
The 2LA and resonance interpretation assumes 514.5 nm (2.41 eV) lies near the WS2 A/B exciton region; the exact exciton energies were not looked up.
The Si ratio (about 10.7x) was not calibrated against a bare SiO2/Si reference, so it only shows that spot 1 is less attenuated than spot 2, not the layer count.
